last_analysis: All nine trials scored exactly 0 on dev and on training success. They differed widely in heads (per-layer, relational, pooled, flat MLP, dense), recipes (1, 2 or 4 epochs, 64 or 256 envs, up to 426k samples) and sizes. Seed noise cannot explain a flat zero this consistent. So a factor shared by all of them is the bottleneck. Two explanations fit. First, the dense reward rewards filling target cells even when a placement seals missing cells below it. The agent then learns greedy filling and never reaches the rare +1 for an exact build, which gamma 0.95 discounts further. Second, the world may differ from its description, for example a different anchor convention, swapped brick orientations or a transposed index. Then every head that assumes top-left anchoring is misaligned, and the flat heads may just learn too slowly. This last round tests both: a head that does not assume alignment and also sees the mask, the same head plus a dense path, and a baseline with a longer horizon.
